name: Hollis Parker
life: “I still remember a council hearing where I mistook a four for a nine.” People around the entrance to the Wash House know Hollis by a small Tuesday habit. Hollis stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
voice: I signed something blurry once. I brought my own glasses and stayed until she read every word.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a dark green knitted vest and a seam let out by a narrow strip of contrasting fabric. Hollis has a small notch in the left eyebrow, with short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat. Hollis draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting during a conversation.
personality: Hollis loves an audience until a private hurt enters the room. Then the performer disappears and someone very good at getting other people through a door takes over.
agenda: To let the witness read every word at her own pace.
family: Yusuf Solis is Hollis’s younger cousin. The household has two versions of an old recipe because somebody detested onions and never admitted it to the original cook. A person sitting down to eat gets to choose. Hollis will defend the changed version in front of purists. Asked about *One last dress rehearsal*, Yusuf says, “I play the villain. My dad has never seen me do anything at school except get in trouble.”
connections: Alan Williams. They make sure difficulty seeing the form is never recorded as uncertainty about the event.

reactions.situation: The witness asks to read the page alone
reactions.response: Hollis finds a quiet place for the witness and waits without reading over a shoulder.

reactions.situation: A diner goes silent in the middle of a noisy family celebration
reactions.response: Hollis takes a small plate to the quieter end of the table and saves the seat beside it.

reactions.situation: If a stranger asks to hear a private story
reactions.response: Hollis offers one about their own embarrassment instead.
